hook: What ancient Egypt did with honey
hook_sub: From a medical scroll written around 1550 BC

slides.t: Honey is the most common ingredient in the plant remedies of the Ebers Papyrus.
It made bitter medicines easier to swallow.
It held ground herbs together as pills.
It was laid on burns and wounds. Never give honey to babies under one year.

end_p: All 155 plant remedies of the Ebers Papyrus in plain English. A history book, not a medical guide.

hook: The plant behind aspirin was in a 1550 BC scroll

slides.t: Willow appears in a wound plaster in the Ebers Papyrus.
Willow bark contains a natural compound called salicin.
Scientists studied salicin in the 19th century.
That work led to aspirin, one of the most used medicines today.

end_p: The plant remedies of ancient Egypt in plain English. A history book, not a medical guide.

hook: Ancient remedy plants that can hurt you

slides.t: Egypt praised the castor plant, but its seeds contain ricin, a deadly poison.
Its oil contains thujone, which can cause seizures.
Berries are likely unsafe as medicine in large doses.
Poisonous autumn crocus looks a lot like saffron crocus.

end_p: Every dangerous plant in the book has a clear safety note.
